summary: Iteration 2 backend regression + EXPANDED endpoint testing for Bachein. 65/65 pytest cases passed (100%) on public URL https://nda-hub-1.preview.emergentagent.com/api. New coverage: Magic link request/consume (auto-create user, invalid token 404, used-token reuse blocked, 15-min token expiry honored via DB inspection), file upload (PDF text extraction working, 8MB cap, auth required), document creation with attached files (AI flags 'Patent-related' & 'Financial data' correctly auto-tagged), face verification (sets flag + audit entry, 403 for sender), full E2E sign flow with face+OTP+voice gates, signed-PDF download (header-auth returns valid %PDF bytes, 400 when unsigned), audit-PDF download (works pre-sign too, supports BOTH Bearer header AND ?token= query param), AI chat (plain, multi-turn persistence, PDF context with extracted-text injection has_pdf=true, ACTION_JSON detection + stripping from reply field), chat session list + history (ACTION_JSON stripped), chat/action send_pdf_email (account holder → sent:true, non-account-holder → sent:false gracefully without 500, password-protected PDF flag, invalid-email 400, unsupported action 400), and user prefs (dark_mode toggle, tier standard/pro/enterprise, invalid tier silently ignored — see minor note). All 34 prior tests still green after updating the legacy send-otp test to pull OTP from Mongo (the API no longer exposes otp_demo — OTP is delivered via email only, which is the correct production behavior).

minor.issue: Invalid tier values (e.g. 'ultra') are silently dropped and the endpoint returns 200 with the previously-stored tier. Spec says it should 'reject invalid tier'. Recommend returning HTTP 400 with a clear message; otherwise clients have no way to know their value was discarded.

Uses get_current_user dependency only — does NOT accept ?token= query param. The expanded spec/agent note requires ?token= support for in-app PDF viewing via Linking.openURL. Currently a Bearer header is mandatory; the audit-pdf sibling endpoint correctly uses get_user_from_query_or_header. Recommend swapping the dependency on this route too.
AI flags treat short tokens too broadly: 'function ', 'def ', 'import ' substrings will tag any HR doc that mentions 'function' as 'Source code'. Consider word-boundary regex.
Response no longer exposes the OTP (correct for prod). Documenting because legacy test had to switch to Mongo lookup.

action_items: Fix signed-pdf endpoint to support ?token= query-param auth (mirror audit-pdf's get_user_from_query_or_header). Required for in-app PDF viewing via Linking.openURL on iOS/Android.
Return HTTP 400 (or at minimum a server-side warning + 422) when PATCH /api/auth/prefs receives an unknown tier value, instead of silently dropping it.
Tighten AI flag heuristics in POST /api/documents (word-boundary matching) to reduce false positives.
Optional: hide otp_code from any /documents response payloads and projection (already excluded in main reads — verified).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 549 → 904 lines. Now well past the 700-line guideline; recommend splitting into routers/ (auth.py, ai.py, chat.py, documents.py, files.py) before next feature addition.
ACTION_JSON parsing in /ai/chat is fragile (regex-free, depends on rfind('}')) — works in practice but a malformed JSON will silently null `action`. Consider logging when parsing fails.
send_pdf_email payload accepts both 'body' and 'content' keys — undocumented. Either pick one or document both.

Magic-token expiry is compared as ISO strings (lexicographic). Works because all isoformat strings include timezone offset, but a future fmt change could break ordering — prefer parsing into datetime.
Pydantic .dict() still in use (line 617 model_dump is fine, but elsewhere — verified clean here). FastAPI on_event('shutdown') still deprecated (line 901) — pre-existing.
JWT_SECRET still default ('bachein-secret-key-change-in-production-2026') — must rotate before prod.
Resend free-tier 403 on non-account-holder is handled gracefully by send_email returning False — verified.
/upload stores entire file as base64 in Mongo (data_base64 field). With 8MB cap and base64 inflation (~10.7MB stored), this is fine for now but consider GridFS/S3 for production scale.
Face/voice/signature base64 payloads truncated to 500k chars in DB — sane safeguard.
